DO NOT MERGE — under review

Implements brief 003 (`docs/briefs/active.md`, base SHA `a6956f7d`). Round 1's verification found two proxy guards that check something other than the property they claim to enforce, both demonstrated to miss a live violation sitting in the commit that introduced them, plus six related SHOULD-FIX/NOTE findings and two additions found after the brief was written. This closes all of them.

## Items 1–2 (the important ones): class vs instance, stated plainly

**Item 1 — vendor-neutrality guard.** Fixed the actual leak (`docs/roles/brain.md:116`, a `` `/status` `` slash-command reference in a file that must work on any vendor's tool). Partially generalized the guard: a slash-command reference has a shared syntax across chat-driven tools (an inline-code span starting with `/`), so that half is now a regex that catches any future instance, verified against the pre-fix text. The rest of the forbidden list (a frontmatter key, a config filename, a settings flag) has no shared syntax across vendors, so it stays an enumerated list of known instances — stated as such in the test's own docstring, not implied to be general.

**Item 2 — anti-restatement guard.** Stripped all three `.claude/agents/*.md` adapters down to genuinely tool-specific facts; they no longer restate the never-merge rule, the inbox unknown-means-unknown rule, or the commit/push/merge restrictions. Fixed the one concrete divergence (`git branch` missing from the adapter's worktree-confirmation list). Replaced the line-count-only guard with three checks — and one of them, `test_adapters_do_not_echo_known_restated_rules`, is honestly **not** a class detector: a content-similarity approach (longest shared word-run) was tried first and measured to fail on this real text — the actually-restated sentences and plainly innocuous duplication ("Read CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md" in both files) land in the same 5–7-word overlap range, so no single threshold separates them. Full reasoning is in that test's docstring. `test_builder_adapters_confirm_step_matches_contract` *is* general within its scope: it extracts every backtick `git ...` command from the paragraph containing "Confirm" in both files and requires the adapter's set to be a superset.

## Items 3–8, and the two brief additions

- **Item 3** — `.githooks/pre-push` silently allowed a push to master from a bare repository (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel` fails there, and the old script exited 0 before even reading stdin). Fixed by making Guard 1 (the protected-ref check) run unconditionally; only Guard 2 (which needs a working tree) now resolves `repo_root`, and warns instead of exiting silently. Reproduced live against throwaway repos in both directions. Also reproduced two more escape hatches (`git -c core.hooksPath=`, `git send-pack`) and documented the full inventory as established, including what's not enumerable.
- **Item 4** — the inbox Stop hook's role mapping defaulted to `"brain"` for any unrecognized worktree name, which is what let a stale (pre-fa881423) checkout collide with Brain's own inbox entry. Now `"brain"` requires a confirmed match against the primary checkout's root; anything else lands in a distinct `unknown-<name>` bucket. Documented plainly that this can't be fixed retroactively for a worktree already detached at a pre-fix commit.
- **Item 5** — `.claude/agents/verifier.md` overclaimed that the `tools:` frontmatter always restricts the seat; hedged to say it only applies on the subagent-dispatch path, not this seat's documented normal interactive launch.
- **Item 6** — new test pins the five required-check names (from a live `gh api .../branches/master/protection` read) against what `.github/workflows/edopro-next.yml` would actually produce, so a rename or dropped matrix leg fails loudly. Documented the residual gap: this can't verify branch protection itself from inside CI.
- **Item 7** — `HistoricalBypassTest`'s three tests all constructed the identical already-resolved stdin line, proving nothing about the resolution step each claimed to test. Rewritten to exercise real `git push` with each exact refspec against a throwaway bare remote.
- **Item 8** — closed the undefined branch in the inbox fallback: repository state can confirm Builder's work happened, but cannot confirm Verifier's (no diff, no commit, no PR). Added a third fallback step to both `docs/roles/README.md` and `docs/agents/launching.md`: ask the owner directly rather than guess.
- **Additions (a)/(b)** — `_tracked_paths()` read `git ls-files` (the index) instead of `git ls-tree -r HEAD` (the committed tree), so a staged-but-uncommitted file could pass locally where a fresh clone of the pushed SHA would fail. Fixed, with a regression test against a disposable repo. The `resolves()` `except ValueError` fallback for an out-of-repo link reverted to a working-tree existence check — exactly the mechanism that caused the original bug. Closed it outright (returns `False`) rather than leaving a documented-but-live copy of the bug.

## Evidence

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`: 69 ran, 0 failures, 10 skipped (client/ not built on this machine — expected, no cmake/Qt here).
- `python tools/generate_messages.py --check` / `generate_protocol_constants.py --check`: both pass.
- Every new or changed guard is mutation-tested; the mutation and resulting failure count for each is in the completion report.
- Did not run any cmake/ctest cycle — this machine has neither cmake nor Qt, and nothing in this brief touches `client/`, `data/`, `policy/`, `ui/`, `gframe/` or `ocgcore/`.

Full completion report (base/head SHAs, every command run, mutation results, bypass-inventory establishment method, and open questions) to follow via the framework's usual handoff.
